lines.dialogue: Sorry, sorry, this boy needed a Cinnabon.
What? Your family's coming over and everyone likes pie.
You like pie.
What, we're buying it.

Yes, Mitchell will be keeping his dental practice and I'll be home full-time, but that does not make me "the wife." Sure, I gained a few pounds while we were expecting the baby, but that was stress. CAMERON (V.O.) (CONT'D) It's perfectly normal. It would be nice if he understood that.
Oh stop worrying.
I guess that's possible.
What the hell is that supposed to mean?
What, that I'm more womanly?
Is there a particular reason you've been in a bitchy mood all day when this is supposed to be the happiest day of our lives?
We'd like to pay for your cat food.
Tada! Your new home! Isn't it gorgeous, except for that robot -- I hate to break it to you, your other daddy is a big nerd.
Oh my God, do you love it?
I had Andre do it while we were gone. Look, that's us.
We're floating above her, always there to protect her.
That is not that gay.
You know what? I've put up with this mood of yours all day. What is your deal?
See when he looks at the floor, Lily? That's what nerdy daddy does when he's lying.
What?
Are you kidding me? Why the hell not?
We left two days later and I packed for you! You wussed out!
But it's the ceiling's that's too gay.
My parents always knew. My mother says she was in labor with me for twenty-nine hours because I came out of the womb like this:
I'm giving you three minutes and then I'm bringing her out.

It’s Mommy and Me class, not a Broadway opening night. MITCHELL We’re going to be judged enough as the only gay parents, I don’t want to be the late ones too. MITCHELL (CONT’D) Really? Pink? Was there something wrong with your fishnet tank top?

Obviously not, I’m wearing it underneath. No, I’m not. Would you relax? MITCHELL I’m sorry, I would just like to make a good first impression. CAMERON You mean fit in? Not terrify the villagers? MITCHELL It’s for Lily. Her future best friend could be in that class and I don’t want to rub anyone the wrong way. Could you just change your shirt? CAMERON Fine, I’ll throw on some khakis and a polo shirt, maybe everyone will think we’re a couple of straight golf buddies who decided to have a kid together.
Yes. Sans Mommy, obviously.
Howdy.

Yes, I know. I’ll tamp down my natural gifts and dance like a straight guy. MITCHELL No slapping your own butt. CAMERON But that’s how I make the horse go. MITCHELL That was very good. CAMERON I feel dirty.
Got the toothpaste and the soap.
I found the diapers. They’re down here.
Where would we keep them?
You want to buy a diaper shed? Are we those guys now? The guys with the diaper shed?

Okay, time to go. MITCHELL So, after charades we went out for coffee and I learned he loved art, played piano, spoke French -- CAMERON Un peu. MITCHELL I misjudged him. CAMERON I’m sort of like Costco. I’m big, I’m not fancy, and I dare you not to like me. MITCHELL And I’m more like... What was the name of that little shop in Paris? CAMERON You are such a snob. GLORIA
What’s going on? PHIL I was in a plane crash.
Oh. That’s nice for Phil.
It’s okay.
He really does.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: He’s at the ten... the five... the one... touchdown!

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: I collect antique fountain pens, I’m quite adept at Japanese flower arrangement -- Ikebana -- and I was a starting center at Missouri State. Surprise! MITCHELL I just don’t like football. CAMERON I’m sorry. I thought part of being in a relationship was pretending to enjoy your partner’s interests. Do you think I really liked home pickle making? MITCHELL Yes, because you did. CAMERON For a week, until we became the weird guys who brought pickles to everyone. “Thanks for inviting us to your lovely home. Here’s a sack of pickles.”

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: I picked up a few things for the party. Is Lily ready?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: What’s wrong?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Go State!

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: That’s our team, the Bears.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Yeah, he’s been studying up.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: So, we’re torn...
You are a cutie. Yes, you are. Are you still baby-proofing?
She is not Donna Summer. She’s clearly Diana Ross from the RCA years. How are you not seeing that?
I made no such promise.

We received, as a baby gift from one of our friends, an adorable baby wig and outfit that made for a great picture and it gave me the idea to dress Lily as various pop icons. I’ve done Olivia Newton John... CAMERON (O.S.) (CONT’D) Madonna, the early years... CAMERON (O.S.) (CONT’D) Stevie Wonder...
It’s sort of taken on a life of it’s own. There’s talk of a coffee table book.
You know what your problem is? You need to loosen up and have fun.
You’ve been tense ever since we brought Lily home. All you do is put child locks on things and read parenting books. Here, hold your daughter. Relax.
Dance with her.
Come on, you know you love this song.
There you go.
Was that her head?
I got boo-boo bear from the freezer.
It was under a pie.
I did what I had to do.
She didn’t cry that much.
Why?
But it’s a dog.
I’m not sure this is as funny as you think it is. Let’s just call your sister.
Mitchell, she’s family. Of course she’s going to be judgmental and condescending.
Well, her head was somewhat protected. DR. MIURA Protected? Was she wearing a hat?
It was a wig. Sort of a ghetto fabulous Afro thing. I thought it might be medically relevant.
By the way, you’ll be pleased to know that Mitchell and I intend to raise Lily with influences from her Asian heritage. DR. MIURA That’s uh... great. Has there been any vomiting since the head bump?

No. We’ve hung some Asian art in her bedroom. And, when she’s ready for solid food, there is a great little pho place close to our house. Am I saying that right? Pho? It’s a soup. DR. MIURA I don’t know. I’m from Denver. We don’t have a lot of pho there.
Thank you. DR. MIURA Denver.
Why?
Mitchell, how long are you going to beat yourself up over one mistake? Is this going to be like the blonde highlights all over again?
What are you talking about? We’re new at this.
But you do so many things I don’t do. You baby-proofed our entire house. You took care of all the adoption paperwork. Without you, we wouldn’t even have a baby to injure.
Which I couldn’t make any sense out of. And you got us on those preschool waiting lists.
See, that’s what makes us a great team. We have different strengths. Who are amazing parents?
I didn’t hear you.
Don’t you forget it.
Don’t worry, Lily! We got this!
I won’t. I won’t.
I’m breaking the window! OPERATOR (V.O.) Emergency Assistance. This is Trina.
I’m breaking it. I swear to God!
Lily! Lily! Daddy’s coming to get you. OPERATOR (V.O.) Sir, we just sent the signal. The doors should be unlocked now.
It’s not unlocked! It’s not -- Oh. That’s amazing.
Any monkey can shoot a “home movie.” I pride myself on making “home films.”
I do not.
That’s not fair --
My thinking was --
That could have been great! Who puts wheels on a crib?!
Or... could this have something to do with... ice skating?
When Mitchell and Claire were kids --
Can I finish? When Mitchell was ten --
-- and Claire was thirteen, they were competitive ice dancers --
He’s still a little angry because Claire quit right before some meet.
So, seeing your dad so proud of Manny didn’t stir up any resentment?
You always do this, instead of letting your feelings out you bury them and they bubble up later in hurtful ways.
What? You love my yellow shirt.
See? Bubbling. Hurtful bubbling. Now you know why I left early that morning.
So, there’s no part of you that wants to clear the air with your sister?

Fine, that’s your family’s way and I’ll respect that. But you should know it’s very hard on people who love you. We feel the tension, we hear the snide words that cut like knives. CLAIRE Hi guys! I brought orange slices. CAMERON I can’t bear this! Claire, Mitchell still resents you for quitting the figure skating team when you were kids. CAMERON (CONT’D) Come on ladies. CLAIRE So, is that what your little jab was about this morning?
